importantFindings: An age cannot determine an exact birthday. Age-only rows and manual age corrections therefore expose and require the exact date before persistence; no approximate birthday is invented.
A manually retyped age is not treated as independent corroboration of the date it was derived from. The exact date must be explicitly confirmed.
The stored date remains the only persisted value and the source for minor/adult rules and compatibility.
Private-photo OCR clears four date flags, not the nine estimated visually on the earlier crop. Remaining low-confidence dates do not have a usable independent age reading and stay flagged.
qolFindings: The exceptional exact-date correction panel adds height only to rows that still need it. Physical use should confirm the wording is clear under time pressure.
Manual create/edit still asks for an exact date because there is no second reading and the storage contract requires it.
evidenceInspected: Five ignored private-photo measurement outputs; only aggregate counts were copied into corroboration-measurement.json
